obligation: Title IV breach report to FSA
citation: SAIG Enrollment Agreement (per DCL GEN-15-18); FSA Cybersecurity Breach Intake
trigger: Actual or suspected breach of student information, or compromise of the College's SAIG or Department system access
deadline: Immediately upon an actual or suspected breach; do not wait for forensic confirmation; update as facts develop
notify: FSA through the Cybersecurity Breach Intake Form (date, impact, method, program contact, OPEID, remediation status) and CPSSAIG@ed.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Title IV participant with a SAIG Enrollment Agreement

trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information involving at least 500 consumers. Unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise; data counts as unencrypted if the key was also accessed
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, electronically on the form at ftc.gov: company name and contact; types of information; date or date range; number of consumers; general description; any law enforcement delay request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company holds customer information on about 2.3 million consumers
clock_starts: Discovery: the first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent other than the person committing the breach (314.4(j)(2))
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with the CISO (Qualified Individual)

trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The FTC notice is still due within 30 days of discovery and must include the determination; law enforcement may request an initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 days on written request
notify: FTC (inside the notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if law enforcement asks

obligation: FERPA record of the unauthorized disclosure
trigger: Personally identifiable information from education records disclosed without authorization
deadline: Record in each affected student's disclosure record, kept as long as the education record is kept. FERPA itself has no breach notification requirement
notify: Internal: the University Registrar records the parties (if known) and the incident; students may inspect the record
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Qualified Individual report to the board
trigger: Any security event
deadline: In the next annual written report; the board risk committee chair is also told the same day for severity-1 incidents (POL-03)
notify: Board risk committee
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents, as each state defines it (definitions, including whether student ID numbers or account credentials are covered, vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state: some say without unreasonable delay; some set a fixed number of days
notify: Affected residents of each state (students, former students, parent borrowers, employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; counsel's state matrix
clock_starts: Varies by state (often determination of a breach)
owner: Chief Privacy Officer with outside counsel

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, or any breach in some states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or other designated regulator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state requires

trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state threshold is met

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company
citation: State breach notification statutes; vendor contracts (POL-01 4.8)
trigger: Vendor that maintains personal information has a breach
deadline: Varies by state; company contracts require 72 hours (legacy contracts and the Title IV servicer are being amended, POAM-005 and POAM-020)
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in contracts

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example, name with SSN, financial account number with access code, or user name or email with password); encrypted data excluded unless the key was also taken
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a)); law enforcement may delay notice by written request (501.171(4)(b))
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. The company's federal rules (Safeguards Rule, FERPA) do not require notice to individuals, so the 501.171(4)(g) deemed-compliance path is not available; counsel to confirm
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only on counsel's advice; unlikely when SSNs or ISIR data were taken

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of the notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendors holding Florida residents' personal information

trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.6)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

trigger: The company determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, incident responders with knowledge, and executives (special blackout notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As early as practical (supports OFAC mitigation and investigation)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until it takes effect. The proposed rule would cover every Title IV institution (N61-R06)

trigger: Incident affecting a partner's LMS tenant, partner students' records, or SL-2 services
deadline: Per partner agreement (standard term: 72 hours for a security incident affecting partner data; 4 hours for a service outage). Each partner is the institution for its own students and decides its own FERPA and state law steps
notify: The 14 partner institutions' designated contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

trigger: Incident affecting the employer portal or sponsored-student data
deadline: Per client agreement (standard term: 72 hours)
notify: About 310 employer clients
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before engaging vendors
notify: Carrier
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI
deadline: n/a
notify: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a covered entity; health information it holds is in FERPA education records, which the definition of PHI excludes (45 CFR 160.103)

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Covered equipment found in use
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts held; recheck if contracts are signed
